core_concepts.name: Degree of a Polynomial
core_concepts.summary: Degree is the highest power of the variable; degree 1 linear, degree 2 quadratic, degree 3 cubic.

core_concepts.name: Zero of a Polynomial
core_concepts.summary: A real number k is a zero if p(k)=0; geometrically it is an x-coordinate where y=p(x) intersects the x-axis.

core_concepts.name: Geometrical Meaning of Linear Zeroes
core_concepts.summary: A linear polynomial ax+b has exactly one zero, equal to the x-coordinate where its straight-line graph cuts the x-axis.

core_concepts.name: Geometrical Meaning of Quadratic Zeroes
core_concepts.summary: A quadratic ax^2+bx+c can have two distinct zeroes, one repeated zero, or no real zero depending on how the parabola intersects the x-axis.

core_concepts.name: Geometrical Meaning of Cubic Zeroes
core_concepts.summary: A cubic can have at most three real zeroes; graph intersections with x-axis correspond to zeroes.

core_concepts.name: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic
core_concepts.summary: If alpha and beta are zeroes of ax^2+bx+c, then alpha+beta = -b/a and alpha beta = c/a.

transfer_links.note: Sum/product of roots reused when solving and constructing quadratic equations.
Quadratic models the height-time path of a thrown object; zeroes are launch/landing times.

core_concepts.name: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Cubic
core_concepts.summary: If alpha beta gamma are zeroes of ax^3+bx^2+cx+d, then alpha+beta+gamma = -b/a, alpha beta+beta gamma+gamma alpha = c/a, alpha beta gamma = -d/a.
